replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics feels like a distant cousin I respect but rarely visit. My parents have high academic expectations, which makes me feel pressure to excel, even though my favorite subjects are computer science and physics. I appreciate its logic but find it less engaging than practical applications in tech.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, absolutely. With my neuroticism score being high, math triggers worry about failing or not meeting my parents' expectations. It's a source of stress, especially when I need to explain complex topics like equations or statistics for work or study.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used an AI tutor once to help with calculus concepts. It was helpful but felt impersonal. Since I prefer hands-on learning and have low openness to new abstract ideas, I found it useful for quick checks but not for deep understanding.

Take the derivative of f(x) with respect to x. Set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are where stationary points occur. Substitute them back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-coordinates.

They help reduce anxiety by offering safe spaces for questions. However, they should supplement, not replace, human teachers who understand student emotions better.
